data.narrative:
Hidden Level, a Series C defense and security company founded by Jeff Cole and Gary Dominicos, has raised $130M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a peer set of 3 same-stage, same-sector comparables in Defense & Security, supplemented by a broader universe of 10 private frontier-tech players (including Anduril Industries and Helsing) and 2 public comps.

Two triangulation methods were applied. Stage-progression analysis, using total raised as a proxy for post-money value, applies a typical 1.7x Series C step-up multiplier to the $130M base, implying $221M. Peer-median analysis across Castelion ($13.0B), Stark Defence ($4.0B), and Neros ($2.5B) yields a median valuation of $4.0B, with a range of $2.5B–$13.0B. The wide dispersion among Defense & Security peers reflects heterogeneity in technology maturity, customer traction, and mission-criticality positioning.

The triangulated analysis supports a range of $188M to $4.6B, with a median of $2.1B. Given Hidden Level's stage and sector, the peer-median method likely carries greater weight than stage-progression in this domain. Key uncertainties include relative differentiation versus named competitors, recurring revenue visibility, and customer concentration within defense budgets. The wide valuation range reflects the nascent, high-variance nature of frontier defense technology.
